q:
Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Punjab is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Haryana is placed in Region 'A'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Nagaland is English.
2. The official language of the State of Mizoram is Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The official language of the State of Telangana is Hindi.
2. Bengali is one of the official languages of the State of Tripura.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The First World Hindi Conference was held at Bhopal in January 1975.
2. The Second World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1976 at Port Louis (Mauritius).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Kannada was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2008.
2. Malayalam was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2008.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Sahitya Akademi, India's national academy of letters, gives its awards for literary works in 24 languages.
2. The Hindi Sahitya Sammelan, a leading organisation for the promotion of Hindi, was founded in the year 1953.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The first Hindi newspaper 'Udant Martand', published from Calcutta in the year 1826, was edited by Bharatendu Harishchandra.
2. 'Prem Sagar', an early prose work in Khari Boli Hindi produced at the Fort William College, was written by Lallu Lal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Gujarati script, though derived from Devanagari, has the headstroke (shirorekha) like the Devanagari script.
2. The Santhali language, included in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution, belongs to the Dravidian family of languages.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President.
2. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, provision is made for the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. In-service Hindi training was made compulsory for Central Government employees by the Presidential Order of 1960.
2. The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Section 7 from Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963?

options.A: Section 7 empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act, while Section 8 deals with the use of Hindi for judgments of High Courts
options.B: Section 7 deals with the use of Hindi, or the official language of a State, in addition to English, for judgments, decrees or orders of a High Court, as authorised by the Governor with the previous consent of the President, while Section 8 empowers the Central Government to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act
options.C: Section 7 deals with the translation of Central Acts into Hindi, while Section 8 deals with the translation of State Acts into Hindi
options.D: Section 7 constitutes the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, while Section 8 provides for the Official Language Commission

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Committee of Parliament on Official Language from the Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee)?

options.A: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language is chaired by the Prime Minister, while the Kendriya Hindi Samiti consists of 30 members of Parliament
options.B: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language is the apex policy-making body for the Official Language, while the Kendriya Hindi Samiti reviews the progress of Hindi and reports to the President
options.C: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language is a statutory body of 30 members of Parliament, constituted under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, which reviews the progress made in the use of Hindi and reports to the President, while the Kendriya Hindi Samiti is the apex policy and advisory body on the Official Language, chaired by the Prime Minister
options.D: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language was set up in the year 1967, while the Kendriya Hindi Samiti was constituted in the year 1976

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Pragya course from the Parangat course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme?

options.A: Pragya is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff, while Parangat is the course prescribed beyond Pragya for staff who require advanced proficiency in Hindi for noting and drafting work
options.B: Pragya is the course prescribed beyond Parangat, while Parangat is the final prescribed course for clerical staff
options.C: Pragya is intended for employees who possess no knowledge of Hindi, while Parangat is intended for employees who have passed the Praveen examination
options.D: Pragya is a course in Hindi stenography, while Parangat is a course in Hindi typewriting

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the constitutional and statutory review bodies for the Official Language is FALSE?

options.A: The Official Language Commission to be constituted under Article 344 of the Constitution consists of a Chairman and other members representing the different languages specified in the Eighth Schedule
options.B: Of the 30 members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language, 20 are drawn from the Lok Sabha and 10 from the Rajya Sabha
options.C: The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is nominated by the President
options.D: The Committee of Parliament on Official Language submits its report to the President, who causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the examinations and incentives under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is FALSE?

options.A: A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award for passing the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks
options.C: Personal pay equal to one increment is admissible to an employee for a period of 12 months on passing the prescribed Hindi examination
options.D: A lumpsum award is admissible to an employee who passes the prescribed examination after undergoing the full prescribed training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the languages in the Eighth Schedule and the classical languages of India is FALSE?

options.A: At the commencement of the Constitution, the Eighth Schedule contained 14 languages
options.B: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali were added to the Eighth Schedule by the Constitution (71st Amendment) Act, 1992
options.C: Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2014
options.D: Tamil was the first language to be declared a 'classical language' by the Government of India

q: A letter in Hindi is received in a Central Government office located in Region 'A'. The dealing assistant proposes to reply in English, on the ground that the contents of the letter are technical in nature. The correct position under the Official Language Rules is:

options.A: The reply may be issued in English, technical letters being exempt from the rule
options.B: The reply is to be issued in the regional language of the State
options.C: The reply may be issued in English if a Hindi translation is attached to the office copy
options.D: The letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi

q: A Central Government office issues its general orders in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union and all its employees know Hindi. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that general orders are required to be issued in:

options.D: Hindi, with an English version to be issued only on demand

q: A Central Government office maintains its website in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that the website of a Central Government office is required to be maintained:

options.C: In the regional language of the State of location only
options.D: In Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form

q: A Central Government office gets its rubber stamps prepared in English only, on the ground that they are used only for internal marking on files. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, the rubber stamps used in a Central Government office should be prepared:

options.B: In Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form

q: At a Central Government office, the name boards and designation boards are displayed in the order: English, Regional language, Hindi. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that name boards, designation boards and sign boards are required to be displayed in three languages, in the order:

A Central Government office sends a communication in Hindi to an office of a State Government located in Region 'C', without enclosing any English translation. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is that a communication issued in Hindi to an office located in Region 'C':

options.A: Is in order, no translation being required for official correspondence
options.B: Must be accompanied by its English translation
options.C: Must be accompanied by its translation in the regional language of that State
options.D: Is in order only if the receiving office is headed by a Hindi-knowing officer

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 66 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award is admissible at this level of marks

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 74 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:
An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 95 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks having been secured
options.B: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 98 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for 24 months

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 90 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 95 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 84 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He passes only if he also secures 88 per cent marks in the theory paper
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.D: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute

q: An employee aged 40 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is compulsory for him, the exemption from compulsory training applying only on attaining the age of 45 years
options.B: The nomination is not in order, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory below the age of 45 years
options.C: The training is optional for him and he may decline it without assigning any reason
options.D: He can be nominated only for the correspondence course conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate

q: In a Central Government office, 81 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 100 per cent of the staff
options.C: The office cannot be notified, notification requiring 90 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office stands automatically notified without any notification in the Official Gazette

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 13,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum of 10,000 words in a year having been exceeded
options.C: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the twelfth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: Personal pay is not admissible in the twelfth month, its period having expired after six months
options.B: Personal pay is admissible for 24 months and the claim is premature
options.C: Personal pay is admissible in the twelfth month only at half the rate of one increment
options.D: Personal pay continues to be admissible in the twelfth month, its total period of admissibility being 12 months

q: A town has twelve Central Government offices. For the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that town:

options.A: No Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted, such a committee requiring at least twenty offices
options.B: The implementation work is to be looked after directly by the Parliamentary Committee on Official Language
options.C: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee can be constituted only if all the offices are notified under Rule 10(4)
options.D: A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is to be constituted, the town having ten or more Central Government offices

q: A Central Government office spends 45 per cent of the total amount spent by it on purchase of books for its office library on Hindi books and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for purchase of books. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, at least 40 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.B: The claim is in order, at least 25 per cent of the amount being required to be spent on Hindi books
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is located in Region 'B'
options.D: The claim is not in order, at least 50 per cent of the amount spent on purchase of books for office libraries being required to be spent on Hindi books

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' originates 95 per cent of its correspondence in Hindi and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for Hindi correspondence. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, the target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The claim is in order, the target for Region 'A' being 75 per cent
options.C: The claim is not in order, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.D: The claim is in order only if the remaining correspondence was issued bilingually

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' originates 60 per cent of its correspondence in Hindi and claims to have complied with the Annual Programme target for Hindi correspondence. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, the target for Region 'C' being 75 per cent
options.B: The claim is not in order, the target for Region 'C' being 100 per cent
options.C: The claim is in order only if the office is notified under Rule 10(4)
options.D: The claim is in order, the target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 60 per cent

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(3) of the Constitution, where a State Legislature has prescribed a language other than English for use in Bills introduced in, or Acts passed by, that Legislature, a translation of the same in English, published under the authority of the Governor in the Official Gazette of the State, shall be deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in the English language.
2. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the members of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The headquarters of the Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) is located at New Delhi.
2. The Central Translation Bureau (Kendriya Anuvad Bureau) was set up in the year 1961.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. World Hindi Day (Vishwa Hindi Diwas) commemorates the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September, 1949.
2. Hindi Pakhwada (Hindi Fortnight) is observed every year in Central Government offices and Railways from 14th September to 28th September.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Third World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1983 at Nagpur.
2. The Fifth World Hindi Conference was held in the year 1996 at London.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 350B of the Constitution, the reports of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities are caused to be laid before each House of Parliament, and sent to the Governments of the States concerned, by the President.
2. The office of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities was set up in the year 1957.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Malayalam was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2013.
2. Odia was accorded the status of a 'classical language' by the Government of India in the year 2013.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The standard of the Praveen course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level.
2. The standard of the Pragya course of the Hindi Teaching Scheme corresponds broadly to the Matriculation (Class X) level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The "Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali" (Comprehensive Glossary of Administrative Terms), the standard reference for Hindi equivalents of administrative terms, is published by the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology.
2. The Hindi translation of Bills introduced in Parliament and of Central Acts is prepared by the Official Language Wing (Rajbhasha Khand) of the Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Chapter III of Part XVII of the Constitution comprises Articles 350 and 351.
2. The Parangat course under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Sanskrit has been declared as the second official language of the State of Uttarakhand.
2. The official language of the State of Haryana is Punjabi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Bihar.
2. Urdu has been declared as the second official language of the State of Telangana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Karnataka is placed in Region 'B'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Kerala is placed in Region 'C'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language is nominated by the President.
2. Personal pay equal to one increment, admissible to an employee on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, is admissible for a period of 24 months.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The recommendations of the first Official Language Commission (Kher Commission) were examined by a Committee of Parliament whose Chairman was G. B. Pant.
2. The first Official Language Commission, appointed in the year 1955, was headed by M. C. Chagla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Munshi-Ayyangar formula on the official language is named after K. M. Munshi and N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar.
2. The Presidential Order of 1960 on the Official Language was issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations under the Hindi Teaching Scheme are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
2. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, meant for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, where the President directs that a language spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State shall be officially recognised, such recognition may be for the whole or any part of the State and for such purposes as he may specify.
2. Under Article 350A of the Constitution, provision is made for the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Gaurav Puraskar of the Department of Official Language was earlier known as the Indira Gandhi Rajbhasha Puraskar.
2. The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield is awarded on Indian Railways to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Punjab is placed in Region 'A'.
2. For the purposes of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the State of Gujarat is placed in Region 'B'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Consider the following statements:
1. 'Prem Sagar', an early prose work in Khari Boli Hindi produced at the Fort William College, was written by Lallu Lal.
2. The first Hindi newspaper 'Udant Martand', published from Calcutta in the year 1826, was edited by Pandit Jugal Kishore Shukla.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 350A from Article 350B of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 350A provides for the appointment of a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, while Article 350B provides for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage
options.B: Article 350A provides that it shall be the endeavour of every State and local authority to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children of linguistic minority groups, while Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President, to investigate matters relating to the safeguards for linguistic minorities
options.C: Article 350A deals with representations for the redress of grievances, while Article 350B deals with the development of Hindi
options.D: Article 350A was inserted by the Constitution (58th Amendment) Act, 1987, while Article 350B formed part of the Constitution as originally enacted

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Article 344 from Article 351 of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 344 lays down the duty of the Union to develop Hindi, while Article 351 provides for the Official Language Commission
options.B: Article 344 deals with the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts, while Article 351 deals with the official language of a State
options.C: Article 344 provides for the authoritative Hindi text of the Constitution, while Article 351 provides for the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.D: Article 344 provides for the constitution of an Official Language Commission and, through the report procedure, of a Committee of Parliament, while Article 351 lays down the duty of the Union to promote the spread of Hindi and to develop it as a medium of expression for the composite culture of India

q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi), Agra from the Central Hindi Training Institute, New Delhi?

options.A: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations, while the Central Hindi Training Institute conducts the correspondence courses in those subjects
options.B: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan functions under the Department of Official Language, while the Central Hindi Training Institute functions under the Ministry of Education
options.C: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan, functioning under the Ministry of Education, is engaged in the teaching of Hindi as a subject, including to non-Hindi speakers and foreign learners, while the Central Hindi Training Institute, functioning under the Department of Official Language, imparts in-service Hindi training to Central Government employees and conducts the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya examinations
options.D: The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan was established in the year 1985, while the Central Hindi Training Institute was established in the year 1955

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the headquarters and parent Ministry of the institutions for the Official Language is FALSE?

options.A: The Department of Official Language functions in the Ministry of Home Affairs
options.B: The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology functions under the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs
options.C: The Central Hindi Directorate functions under the Ministry of Education
options.D: The Central Translation Bureau functions as a subordinate office of the Department of Official Language

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the observance of Hindi Diwas, Hindi Pakhwada and World Hindi Day is FALSE?

options.A: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14th September and was celebrated for the first time in the year 1953
options.B: Hindi Pakhwada is observed every year from 14th September to 28th September
options.C: World Hindi Day is observed on 10th January and was observed for the first time in the year 2006
options.D: World Hindi Day commemorates the adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union by the Constituent Assembly on 14th September, 1949

q: Which one of the following statements relating to the language of the subordinate courts and the official languages of the States is FALSE?

options.A: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Maharashtra is Hindi
options.B: The language of the subordinate (district) courts in the State of Haryana is Hindi
options.C: The official language of the State of Nagaland is English
options.D: The official language of the State of Chhattisgarh is Hindi

q: A Central Government office gets its letter-heads printed in English only, on the ground that all its officers work in English. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads used in a Central Government office are required to be printed in:

options.C: Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form
options.D: The regional language of the State of location and English

q: At a railway station, the reservation charts (list of passengers) are displayed in Hindi and English only, the regional language of the area being omitted altogether. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that the reservation charts displayed at railway stations are printed in:

options.A: Three languages — the regional language, Hindi and English
options.C: The regional language and English only

q: A Central Government office circulates 'Trains at a Glance', the All India Railway Time Table, in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that 'Trains at a Glance' is published in:

options.D: The regional language, Hindi and English

q: A Central Government office finalises a press communique and proposes to issue it in Hindi only, on the ground that Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. Under Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963, the correct position is that the press communique is required to be issued in:

options.B: The regional language of the State of location only

q: A Central Government office publishes its part of the Gazette of India in English only, on the ground that the subscribers concerned are English-knowing. Under the Official Language Policy, the correct position is that the Gazette of India is published in:

options.D: Hindi, with an English version issued only on demand

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 69 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award is admissible at this level of marks

q: An employee passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 53 per cent marks. The cash award admissible to him is:

options.D: No cash award is admissible, the lowest slab of the cash award beginning at 55 per cent marks

q: An employee passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 98 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 99 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he has also passed the Pragya examination
options.C: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks having been secured
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for 24 months

q: An employee passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme securing 87 per cent marks. In this case:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent or more marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent or more marks
options.D: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 83 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He fails, the prescribed speed being 90 words per minute
options.B: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 80 words per minute
options.C: He fails, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.D: He passes only if he also secures 88 per cent marks in the theory paper

q: An employee aged 38 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The nomination is not in order, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory below the age of 45 years
options.B: The training is optional for him and he may decline it without assigning any reason
options.C: He can be nominated only for the correspondence course conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate
options.D: The training is compulsory for him, the exemption from compulsory training applying only on attaining the age of 45 years

q: An employee aged 48 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for compulsory in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: The training is compulsory for him at every age
options.B: He can be compelled to undergo the training only during the last year of his service
options.C: The training is not compulsory for him, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory for an employee who has attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He can be nominated only with the prior approval of the Department of Official Language

q: In a Central Government office, 89 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 100 per cent of the staff
options.C: The office cannot be notified, notification requiring 90 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: The office stands automatically notified without any notification in the Official Gazette

q: In a Central Government office, 77 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 75 per cent or more of the staff
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion of 80 per cent or more of the staff not having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office can be notified with the special approval of the Department of Official Language
options.D: The office stands automatically notified on crossing 75 per cent of the staff

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 16,000 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
